base_properties.human_readable: QWERTY Keyboard Layout as Natural Standard

stakeholders.name: keyboard_manufacturers
stakeholders.situation: Produce keyboards in a single layout standard, avoiding retooling costs and inventory complexity. QWERTY's universality means they face no market pressure to support alternatives; the layout's persistence as 'natural' protects their capital investment in existing production lines and eliminates competitive pressure from layout innovation.

stakeholders.name: typing_instruction_industry
stakeholders.situation: Teach QWERTY as the universal standard. Curriculum materials, certification programs, and instructor training are all built around one layout. Alternative layouts would require complete curriculum replacement and instructor retraining; QWERTY's status as 'the way keyboards work' eliminates that cost and forecloses competitive entry from alternative-layout instruction.

stakeholders.name: legacy_software_vendors
stakeholders.situation: Maintain software systems with QWERTY hardcoded into interfaces, keyboard shortcuts, and user expectations. Layout flexibility would require internationalization-grade abstraction layers; treating QWERTY as natural avoids that engineering cost and protects installed-base lock-in.

stakeholders.name: alternative_layout_advocates
stakeholders.situation: Promote ergonomically optimized layouts (Dvorak, Colemak, others) and document efficiency gains in controlled studies. They are structurally excluded from the coordination conversation: QWERTY's naturalization means their proposals are treated as hobbyist curiosities rather than engineering improvements, and no institutional actor has incentive to test them at scale.

stakeholders.name: new_typists
stakeholders.situation: Learn QWERTY because it is the only layout available on standard equipment and the only one taught in schools. They bear the ergonomic and efficiency costs of a layout optimized for 19th-century mechanical constraints that no longer apply, but have no choice set: switching to an alternative layout means relearning from scratch with no institutional support and incompatibility with every shared keyboard.

stakeholders.name: ergonomics_researchers
stakeholders.situation: Study typing efficiency, repetitive strain injury rates, and layout optimization. They document that QWERTY is suboptimal by modern ergonomic standards and that alternatives reduce injury rates and increase speed in controlled conditions, but their findings do not propagate into institutional practice because the naturalization narrative forecloses the question.

six_questions.coordination_function: Provides a universal keyboard layout so that any typist can use any keyboard and any keyboard works with any software without configuration.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves the cost of layout suboptimality (slower typing, higher injury rates, learning difficulty) from manufacturers and institutions to individual typists, who bear ergonomic and efficiency costs in exchange for universal compatibility.
six_questions.absent_voices: Alternative layout advocates and ergonomics researchers are systematically excluded from the standards conversation; their proposals are dismissed as impractical because QWERTY is already universal, which is the condition the constraint itself maintains.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: If QWERTY's status as 'natural' disappeared and layout choice became a live question, manufacturers would face competitive pressure to offer alternatives, typing instruction would diversify, software would need layout abstraction, and individual typists would face a real choice set with efficiency/ergonomics tradeoffs visible.
six_questions.founding_problem: Early typewriters jammed when adjacent keys were struck in rapid succession; QWERTY separated common letter pairs to slow typists down and prevent mechanical jams.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: The mechanical jamming problem was solved by the 1910s with improved typewriter mechanisms and disappeared entirely with electronic keyboards in the 1970s. This is uncontested historical fact documented by typewriter historians and mechanical engineers outside any benefiting party. Ergonomics researchers and alternative-layout advocates attest the founding problem is dead; keyboard manufacturers and typing instruction industry do not dispute the historical facts but argue the coordination function now justifies persistence.

commentary.narrative_context:
QWERTY keyboard layout emerged in the 1870s to solve a mechanical problem in early typewriters. That problem was solved by the 1910s and disappeared entirely with electronic keyboards, but QWERTY persists as the universal standard. The constraint is CLAIMED as mountain (natural coordination standard) while the metrics describe low but accumulating extraction and the structural data identifies beneficiaries whose costs would rise if the layout became contestable. This is deliberate FSM authoring: the claim represents the naturalization narrative ('QWERTY won because it works'), the metrics and beneficiary structure represent the alternative reading ('QWERTY persists because changing it is costly for organized actors'). The engine measures the divergence.

KEY AGENTS (by structural relationship):
- keyboard_manufacturers: Primary beneficiary (organized/mobile) — avoid retooling costs
- typing_instruction_industry: Primary beneficiary (organized/mobile) — avoid curriculum replacement
- legacy_software_vendors: Primary beneficiary (institutional/constrained) — avoid abstraction layer costs
- new_typists: Primary target (powerless/trapped) — bear ergonomic and efficiency costs
- alternative_layout_advocates: Excluded (moderate/constrained) — structurally foreclosed from standards conversation
- ergonomics_researchers: Analytical observer (moderate/analytical) — document suboptimality without institutional uptake
commentary.logic_rationale: Extraction is low but rising (0.08 → 0.18 over 120 years) because the layout's suboptimality becomes more costly as typing volume increases and ergonomic knowledge advances, while the beneficiaries' coordination story remains unchanged. Suppression is low (0.22) because the constraint operates primarily through naturalization rather than active enforcement: no one prohibits alternative layouts, but institutional inertia and network effects make them unviable. Theater is very low (0.12) because the coordination function is real and the naturalization narrative is sincerely believed by most participants. Accessibility collapse is high (0.78) because once QWERTY is universal, learning an alternative means incompatibility with every shared keyboard and every other typist. Resistance is low (0.15) because the constraint is experienced as natural fact rather than imposed rule, and the costs are diffuse and individualized.
commentary.directionality_logic: Manufacturers, typing instruction, and software vendors are structural beneficiaries: QWERTY's naturalization protects their capital investments and forecloses competitive pressure from layout innovation. They have mobile or constrained exit (could support alternatives but choose not to) and sit near the beneficiary end of directionality. New typists are the primary targets: they bear the ergonomic and efficiency costs with no choice set, trapped exit, and sit near the target end. Alternative layout advocates are excluded rather than coordinated. Ergonomics researchers are analytical observers.
commentary.perspectival_gap: From the beneficiary seats (manufacturers, instruction, software), QWERTY is a genuine natural standard that emerged from competitive selection and persists because it solves the coordination problem efficiently. From the target seat (new typists), the same structure operates as a locked-in suboptimal standard that imposes unnecessary costs. From the excluded seat (alternative advocates), QWERTY is an extractive arrangement maintained by institutional inertia that forecloses superior alternatives. The engine computes these divergences from the structural data; the authored mountain claim does not adjudicate between them.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The founding problem (mechanical jamming) is dead, but the constraint persists and its extraction is accumulating. This is the mandatrophy signature: a coordination function that outlived its original justification and now operates primarily to protect beneficiaries' sunk costs. The naturalization narrative ('QWERTY is just how keyboards work') prevents the question of layout choice from being asked, which is how the extraction remains invisible. The six-questions genealogy interview surfaces this: founding_problem_status is 'dead' (uncontested), disappearance_verdict is 'world_rearranges' (arrangements depend on it), and the gap between them is the mandatrophy the classification system exists to detect.

omegas.question: Is QWERTY's persistence a natural outcome of genuine coordination efficiency, or a constructed outcome maintained by beneficiaries' sunk costs and institutional inertia?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Large-scale natural experiment: jurisdiction mandates layout choice in public procurement and education, measures adoption rates of alternatives and efficiency outcomes over a generation. If alternatives gain substantial market share and show efficiency gains, the persistence is constructed; if QWERTY remains dominant despite choice, the persistence is natural.
omegas.impact: If natural, the constraint is a genuine mountain and the beneficiaries are incidental. If constructed, the constraint is a false summit (tangled rope or rope with accumulating extraction) and the beneficiaries are structural.
omegas.description: Whether QWERTY's universality is natural coordination or constructed lock-in.

omegas.question: Does QWERTY persist because network effects make individual switching costly (natural coordination), or because institutional actors actively prevent alternatives from reaching the scale where network effects could flip (constructed protection)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Historical analysis of alternative layout adoption attempts: if alternatives failed despite reaching viable user bases and demonstrating efficiency gains, institutional protection is operative. If alternatives never reached viable scale despite being available, network effects alone explain persistence.
omegas.impact: If network effects alone, the extraction is the unavoidable cost of coordination and the beneficiaries are incidental. If institutional protection, the beneficiaries are actively maintaining the arrangement and the extraction is avoidable.
omegas.description: Whether persistence is passive (network effects) or active (institutional foreclosure).

omegas.question: What is the actual ergonomic and efficiency cost of QWERTY relative to optimized alternatives, measured in injury rates, typing speed, and learning time?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Meta-analysis of controlled ergonomic studies comparing QWERTY to Dvorak, Colemak, and other alternatives across diverse typing tasks and user populations.
omegas.impact: If the cost differential is negligible, the extraction is low and the mountain claim is supported. If the cost differential is substantial, the extraction is higher than the low base metric suggests and the false summit reading is supported.
omegas.description: Magnitude of the ergonomic cost QWERTY imposes.

omegas.question: Are the identified beneficiaries genuine structural beneficiaries who would act to maintain QWERTY if it were threatened, or are they artifacts of a search process that finds beneficiaries by construction whenever a universal standard exists?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Counterfactual test: if a jurisdiction mandated layout choice, would the identified beneficiaries lobby against it or accept it? Historical evidence from past standardization contests in adjacent domains (measurement systems, electrical standards) where similar beneficiaries either defended or accepted change.
omegas.impact: If the beneficiaries would not act to defend QWERTY, they are search artifacts and the mountain claim is supported. If they would defend it, they are structural beneficiaries and the false summit reading is supported.
omegas.description: Whether beneficiary identification is structural or artifactual.

network.dual_formulation_note: This constraint is authored as a single reading (the naturalization reading: QWERTY as mountain). The alternative reading (QWERTY as constructed lock-in maintained by beneficiaries) would be a separate constraint story with higher extractiveness, explicit beneficiary/victim structure, and tangled_rope or rope classification. The two readings share the same observable (QWERTY's universality) but interpret its persistence differently, which is the kernel contest the FSM machinery exists to detect.
